newsitem.title: JORDAN: Human rights group urges Kuwait to release detainees.
newsitem.headline: Human rights group urges Kuwait to release detainees.

text.p: The Arab Organisation for Human Rights in Jordan urged Kuwait on Thursday to release Jordanian prisoners after reports of beatings in a Kuwaiti jail.

The organisation said it had received a report that 400 Kuwaiti security men carrying clubs and sticks beat inmates for three hours in a wing of Salbiya prison in Kuwait housing more than 100 prisoners.
It did not say whether it had been able to verify the report.
Kuwait has dismissed reports of the beatings as "lies".
A Jordanian official said the government, which has had no embassy in Kuwait since the two countries fell out during the 1990-91 Gulf War, was trying to check the report through third parties.

The human rights group said according to its report around 400 men from Kuwait's special forces "entered the prisoners' area and hit them for three hours without any intervention from prison authorities".
It said they were then left outside in the cold for three hours. Their money, belongings and books were taken, it said.

A relative of one of the detainees, who asked not to be named, said three prisoners were still in hospital one week after the alleged beatings, which he said took place on Tuesday or Wednesday last week.

He named two of them as Zuheir Omar Saleh, born in 1954 and serving a 15-year sentence, and Mamoun Mohammed Ahmed, born in 1968 and serving a life sentence for collaboration with Iraqi forces during their seven-month occupation of the emirate.
Kuwait said on Thursday reports of the beatings were aimed at "defaming the state of Kuwait".

"Kuwait is extremely keen on safeguarding human rights guaranteed by our Islamic religion," a Kuwaiti official said, noting that officials from the International Committee of the Red Cross have unconditional access to Kuwaiti prisons.
Kuwait's ties with Jordan were strained over Amman's sympathy for Iraq during the seven-month occupation of the oil-rich Gulf Arab state.
